column1: # Motion Prompt catalog (en) · 120 elements · https://motion-prompt.2077tech.com/ · columns: id
column6: summary
An app icon pops in with a bounce, then a notification badge pops in a moment later.
Chart bars rise one after another from the left, each slightly delayed.
A like heart fills in, and a ring, lines and dots burst outward at the same moment.
A chart line draws itself on, and is later erased from its starting end.
Headline text slides out from behind an invisible edge marked by a single line.
Text is typed into an input field one character at a time, then the send button lights up and is pressed.
A number races upward and locks onto its final value.
Words move the way they mean: one stretches, one bounces, one spins, one slams down.
Two squares cover the same distance in the same time: the top one at constant speed, the bottom one eased.
A gauge needle swings past its target, comes back and settles.
A bouncing character squashes on landing and stretches as it takes off.
A shape changes smoothly from circle to square to star to heart, with its colour.
A blob stretches out, breaks into drops and merges back into one.
A ball moving in a figure eight leaves a fading trail of copies behind it.
Particles keep shooting up from an emitter, spread out and fall.
A landscape pans sideways; near layers move more and far layers move less, creating depth.
A circle- or star-shaped window grows, showing the next scene inside it.
Coloured bands sweep across and cover the frame; when they leave, the next scene is there.
Paint-like liquid drips down from the top and fills the frame, becoming the next scene.
The camera pushes into the hole of a letter O and comes out in the next scene.
A card turns over around its vertical axis and shows its other side.
A band of light crosses the surface of a logo badge at an angle.
Text slices shift sideways, colours split and small bars appear, with no brightness flashing.
A heavy headline slab drops with a thud and the whole frame shakes from the impact.
The camera stays in place and pivots from left to right; because it is a rotation, near and far layers slide sideways by the same amount.
The camera stays in place and pivots upward, from a person at ground level up to the top of a tower.

column5: dolly,dolly in,push in,track in,move forward,parallax,camera move
column6: The camera itself moves toward the subject; near objects grow and pass quickly while the distant mountains barely change.
The camera does not move; only the focal length gets longer, so the whole picture enlarges by the same ratio.
The camera moves sideways at the same speed as a walking person; the person stays centred while nearer posts sweep past faster.
The camera travels on a circle around the subject; the person stays centred while the trees and buildings behind sweep sideways.
The camera rises while tilting down until it looks down on the person.
The camera pulls back while zooming in by the same ratio; the person keeps the same size and only the background closes in.

column5: rack focus,focus pull,pull focus,depth of field,blur,bokeh,foreground
column6: The camera does not move; focus shifts from a flower in the foreground to a person behind it, swapping which one is blurred.
Adds a small, irregular shake to the whole frame, as if the camera were held by hand instead of on a tripod.

column4: FPV drone shot (FPV 穿越机镜头)
column6: A first-person view flying low and fast between two rows of trees, banking from side to side.
A level camera rolls around its lens axis and holds with the horizon on a diagonal.
In front of a fixed camera a person rises and falls slowly through a jump while leaves drift down slowly; the whole action is stretched out.

column5: speed ramp,time remap,ramping,fast to slow,variable speed,velocity
column6: Within one shot the playback speed changes smoothly from fast to slow; a graph at bottom left shows the speed.
With a fixed camera, 06:00 to 18:00 is compressed into a few seconds; sun, clouds, people and shadows move in fast forward.
The picture stops at the moment a jumping person reaches the top, then resumes from the same frame 1.4 s later.
Camera position and framing stay the same while the person's position and the clock jump; time is skipped inside one scene.
A thrown ball becomes, in the next shot, a sun at the same position and size; two different scenes are joined on a matching shape.
The camera swings sideways very fast and the next scene is swapped in during the streaked blur.
The next picture is laid over the current one and its opacity rises until it takes over; both show through each other midway.
A vertical edge moves from left to right and the next picture replaces the current one behind it.
A quiet scene of a person asleep cuts with no warning straight to an intense one; the volume meter jumps at the same moment.

column5: j-cut,j cut,split edit,audio lead,sound first,audio transition,edit
column6: The next scene's audio starts before the picture changes; the picture is shown on top with video and audio timelines below.

column5: l-cut,l cut,split edit,audio lag,sound carries over,audio transition,edit
column6: The previous scene's audio carries on for a while after the picture has changed; the picture is shown on top with video and audio timelines below.
Clicking "Open" dims the whole page and a small window scales up slightly into the centre; clicking × closes it.
Clicking "Menu" slides a tall panel in from the left; clicking outside slides it back.
A finger taps "View details" and a panel rises from the bottom; dragging its handle down closes it.
Clicking the first of three headings opens its content and pushes the rows below down; clicking again closes it.
Clicking the field opens four options below it; picking "Nagoya" closes the list and fills the field.
Hovering over a "?" icon shows a short note in a dark bubble above it; it disappears when the cursor leaves.
Clicking "Details" opens a small white panel to its right with a pointer at the button; clicking OK inside closes it.
Clicking "Save" slides a dark notice into the bottom-right corner; when its time bar runs out it slides away.
Clicking the tabs "Overview, Pricing, Reviews" in turn slides a blue underline across and swaps the content below.
Each click on the right arrow slides a row of three different images one step to the left, and the dot below moves.
The switches on the first two of three setting rows are turned on in turn, then off again.
Clicking Day, Week or Month slides a blue highlight across and the bar chart below changes height.
Clicking the "New" and "Free" chips adds a check mark and turns them blue, and cards that do not match fade out.
On a price slider, the left handle is dragged right and the right handle left to narrow the range, then both go back.
Pressing + three times raises the number from 1 to 4, and pressing − three times brings it back to 1; the number pops on each press.
Clicking 2 and then 3 in the page numbers moves the blue circle and swaps the list above; finally it goes back to 1.
Clicking the three-line icon at the header's right turns it into ×, and a menu drops down from under the header; clicking again closes it.
Clicking "Courses" in the breadcrumbs goes up to the list page; clicking a card there returns to the detail page.
Hovering over "Products" in the header drops a full-width panel with three columns of links and an image; it closes when the cursor leaves.
Each click on "Next" turns the next of four step circles into a check and extends the blue line to the following step.
Clicking reload turns the list into grey blocks of the same shape with a sweeping shine; the content returns when loading ends.
Clicking "Send" washes the card white and a blue arc spins in the middle; when finished it changes to a check and fades.
Each time a notification arrives, the blue dot on the bell in the header counts up 1, 2, 3; clicking the bell clears it.
Deleting the two list rows with their trash icons brings up an empty-box drawing, "Nothing here yet" and an "Add" button.
As the page scrolls down, the headline moves up normally while the sky and sun, far hills and near hills move more slowly.
As the page scrolls, the heading, the cards and the body text each rise into place and fade in when they enter the view.
The announcement strip scrolls away, but the header below it stops at the top edge and the content scrolls underneath.
A navy section stops when it fills the view; further scrolling steps the number and photo through 1→2→3, then the section scrolls on.
As the page scrolls down, the section holds still and four numbered work cards travel to the left.
After a small scroll, the page carries itself the rest of the way until the next section's top lines up with the top of the view.
As the article is read a bit at a time, the line along the top grows from the left and reaches the far end at the bottom of the page.
As the copy scrolls into view, a yellow highlighter stroke is drawn left to right across the lower half of the key words.
Only the card under the cursor lifts slightly and its shadow spreads; it settles back when the cursor leaves.

column4: Image zoom on hover (悬停图片缩放)
column6: The photo under the cursor slowly enlarges while its frame stays the same size, and shrinks back when the cursor leaves.
As the cursor moves around the page, an orange circle follows it a little behind.
As the cursor comes near, the button is drawn toward it and follows; when the cursor leaves, the button wobbles back to its place.
Each click sends a white circle out from the click point to fill the button, then it fades away.
Under the link the cursor is on, an orange line grows from the left; when the cursor leaves, the line shrinks away to the right.
Dragging the line in the middle of the photo left and right changes how much of the grey "before" (left) and the coloured "after" (right) is shown.
When the cursor heads out through the top of the page (toward the tabs and close button), the page dims and a "Wait!" popup opens. The × closes it.
On a navy screen the number under the logo counts from 0% to 100%; then the screen lifts away and the page underneath fades in.
As grey placeholders scroll into view, a spinner turns in each, and the images fade in as they arrive. The top row is loaded from the start.
Scrolling down to the end of the list brings up a spinner, then three new items are added so reading can go on.
Clicking a card in the work list sweeps an orange panel across from the left; the URL changes and the panel exits to the right on the detail page. "Back to list" returns the same way.
Clicking "Pricing" in the menu glides the page down to the pricing section; the up arrow at the bottom right glides it back to the top.
Inside a navy band, large service names separated by orange dots keep moving to the left without a gap.
Behind the headline, soft patches of orange, light orange, blue and light blue drift in circles and keep blending differently.
Next to the headline, a phone, a heart badge and a rating chip each bob gently out of step, and the shadow under the phone grows and shrinks.
The sun moves from outside the frame to directly behind the person's head; a thin bright edge appears around the figure, a pale warm haze covers the frame and the side facing the camera darkens.

The surroundings go dark and two lights behind the person, left and right, draw thin bright edges only along both sides of the head and shoulders; the plan at the bottom right shows where the two lights are.
As the exposure is set for the bright evening sky, the person, buildings, lamp and tree turn into flat black shapes with no detail and only the sky stays bright.
The light swings from near the front (20°) to directly at the side (90°); the shadow on the head grows from a crescent to exactly half, splitting the face down the middle.
A light 45° to the side and 45° up comes on; the right side of the face falls into shadow except for a small inverted triangle of light on the shadow-side cheek.

column5: butterfly lighting,paramount lighting,beauty lighting,portrait lighting,overhead light,glamour
column6: A light in front of the face and high above comes on; the face lights evenly on both sides and only a small symmetrical shadow falls under the chin.

column5: golden hour,magic hour,sunset light,warm light,long shadows,low sun
column6: The sun drops to just above the horizon; sky and ground turn orange, the left side of the person lights up and the shadows of the lamp and tree stretch far to the right.
Once the sun has set, the sky turns two bands of deep blue, the windows and street lamp come on in amber and the person becomes a dark blue shape.

column5: bokeh,shallow depth of field,background blur,wide aperture,f/1.4,out of focus,lights
column6: As the aperture opens, the in-focus person stays sharp, the buildings behind soften and the street lamps and distant lights spread into large, pale discs.

column5: tilt-shift,miniature,miniature effect,fake miniature,selective focus,toy town,focus band
column6: The top and bottom bands of the street blur while only the middle band with the road, the car and the small people stays in focus, so the street looks like a model.

column5: long exposure,light trails,slow shutter,night photography,car trails,motion
column6: The street turns to night; the moving car fades to almost nothing, a red tail-light line stretches out behind it and white and amber lines run along the opposite lane.
The camera follows the moving car: the car stays sharp in the middle of the frame while only the buildings, trees and lamps behind it streak sideways.
As the sun comes out from behind a building, rays appear around it and a line of light dots, hexagons and a ring runs from the sun through the centre of the frame to the opposite side.
The middle of the street scene bulges out; the vertical lines of the buildings and the lines of the road bow outward while the corners stay where they are.

The street scene is split into red, green and blue and the three are laid back together at slightly different sizes, so red and cyan fringes appear on the edges of the person, buildings and lamps, larger towards the sides.
The frame darkens smoothly from the corners while the person and the road in the middle stay bright.
The landscape and the person turn to light, near-white colours with very faint shadows, and the hump of the histogram at the bottom right moves to the right end.
Most of the frame sinks into darkness and the sun goes out; only the right edge of the bust, lit from the side, stays bright. The histogram hump moves to the left end.
The colour drains from the same landscape; the sun and the light on the figure turn grey and the shapes read only by their brightness.
The colours of the same landscape are replaced by a range between just two colours: indigo in the darks and pink in the lights.

column5: teal and orange,orange and teal,cinematic,color grading,blockbuster,film look
column6: In the same landscape the sky, hills, ground and the shadowed figure shift to teal while the sunlit edge of the figure and the sun shift to orange, a complementary contrast.
Fine grain appears over the whole of the same landscape and the colours lean slightly towards a warm cream.
From the right edge of the same landscape a band of leaked light comes in, pale yellow on the inside and red at the edge, swaying slowly.
The background turns white and the landscape of hills, house, trees and sun appears, scaled down, only inside the shape of the bust.
